And when he had…spoken, he spat on the ground, and made clay of…spittle, and he anointed the eyes of the blind man with the clay, And said unto him, Go wash in the pool of Siloam, (that is by interpretation, Sent.) He went his way therefore, and washed, and came seeing. The neighbors therefore, when they which before had seen him that he was blind, said, Is not this he that set and begged? Some said, This is he: others said, He is like him: but he said, I am he. Therefore said they unto him, How were thine eyes opened? He answered and said, A man that is called Jesus made clay, and anointed my eyes, and said unto me, Go…wash in the pool of Siloam, and wash: and I went and washed, and I received my sight. Then said they unto him, Where is he? He said, I know not. They brought…the Pharisees to him that beforetime was blind. And it was the sabbath day when Jesus made the clay, and anointed his eyes. Then again the Pharisees also asked him how is it that thou has received thy sight. He said unto them, He that—He put clay on my eyes, and I washed, and do see. Therefore said some of the Pharisees, This man is not of God, because he keeps not the sabbath day. Others said, How can a man that is a sinner do such miracles? And there was a division among them. They said unto the blind man again, What sayest thou of him, that he has opened thine eyes? And he said, He is a prophet. But the Jews did not believe concerning him, that he had been blind, and received his sight, until they called his parents of him that had received his sight. And they asked them, saying, Is this your son, who you say that was born blind? how then doth he now see? His parents answered them and said, We know that this is our son, and that he was born blind: But by what mean he now seeth, we know not; or who has opened his eyes, we know not: he is of age; ask him: he shall speak for himself. These words spake the parents, because they feared the Jews: for the Jews had agreed already, that if any man did confess that he was the Christ, he should—they should be put out of the synagogue. Therefore said his parents, He’s of age; ask him. Then again called they the man that was blind, and said unto him, Give God the praise: we know that this man is a sinner. He answered and said, Whether he be a sinner or no, I know not: but one thing I know, that, whereas I was once blind, I now see. Then said they unto him again, What did he do unto thee? how opened he thine eyes? He answered them, I have told you already and you did not hear: wherefore would you hear it again? to…also be his disciples? Then they reviled him, and said, Thou art his disciple; but we are Moses’ disciples. We know that God spake unto Moses: as for this fellow, we know not…whence he is. The man answered and said unto them, Why here ye this marvelous thing, that you know not from whence he is, and yet he has opened mine eyes. Now we know that God heareth not sinners: but if any man be a worshipper of God, and doeth his will, he will hear him—hear it. Since the world began is it not heard that any man has opened…one that was born blind. If this man were not of God, he could do nothing. Then answered and said…They answered and said unto him, Thou art altogether borned in sin, and does thou teach us? And they cast him out. Then Jesus heard that they had cast him out; and when he… found him, he said unto him, Dost thou now believe…the Son of God? He answered and said, Who is he, Lord, that I may believe on him? Jesus said unto him, Thou has both seen him, and it is he that talketh with thee. And he said, Lord, I believe. And he worshipped him.

What a marvelous occasion. A man born blind, Jesus opened his eyes. And then the people didn’t believe, it and they was questioning him, what he did about it. He only did what Jesus told him to do. And if any person will do what Jesus tells them to do, he will receive just what you have need of, if you’ll just believe. Do you believe that? May the Lord add His blessings now, as we start to pray for the sick. All right. I believe Billy met me there on the stairway a while ago, and said he give out prayer cards A-50 to a hundred. And let’s start praying for the sick. And we won’t keep you no longer than we can help. Maybe a little later on in the week, it’ll get a little cooler. And then we’ll press right into it with everything that we have. Let’s be in prayer.

How many in here believes God’s going to hear tonight and answer prayer? Oh, isn’t that wonderful? Brother Lindsay, that was a mighty nice then to see a solid ground there of—of every person believing—on believing grounds. Anything could happen. Now, the one thing I’m going to ask you to do, is…How many has faith that Jesus Christ has risen from the dead and is manifesting Hisself right here among us? Do you believe that? [Congregation says, “Amen.”—Ed.] Well, now, all the faith you have will never do no good until you get some works with it. Is that right? You’ve just got to say now, “I believe it. I accept it. That settles it. And here I am.” See? That’s it. That—that settles the whole thing. All right.

Let’s not call too many at once. We get usually fifty or a hundred up here, and they stand in line and get so tired. Let’s take…Who’s got prayer card A-50? Let’s see your hand. Prayer card A-50? Look on the back of a little card and you’ll see it has got a number there. And your name’s on the front of it. A-50? Is that here? Raise up your hand, ever who has it. A-50? 51? I thought I got the wrong letter may…51, who has prayer card A-51? 52? Raise up quickly when you can. 52, 53, 54, A-55, 56, 57, 58, 59, 60? Did you give out A’s, son? What say? Oh, they’re raising their hand…All right. I just thought…I didn’t see the hands myself; I’m sorry. All right. I—I started at A-50. Yes. I got A-50, A-51, 52, on down. I got up to sixty now. Let’s see what we got now, 60. Now, you take your places.

You know, I’m so thankful, that as far as I know there’s only been one person that I know of that come in the building that was crippled, what God hasn’t healed, except this lady setting right here. And I’ve watched. I know what’s wrong with her. And I know what’s happened. But I’m just waiting to see the time when she’s healed then I’ll call her. Because she’s been faithfully coming. There’s been a little girl setting there. But all the cots, and stretchers, and the cripples, and everything has been healed and walked out in the meeting. Isn’t that marvelous? Everyone that they brought…All right.

Now, what we got, up to fifty? To sixty I believe, wasn’t it? All right. Let’s—let’s go to seventy then. Seventy-five, let’s make that: A-50 to 75, and see…Don’t get too many in the line. Then we’ll maybe get some more, just in a few moments. Blest be the tie that binds Our hearts in Christian love; The fellowship of kindred mind Is like to that above. We share our mutual woes, Our mutual burdens bear; And often for each other flows A sympathizing tear. When we asunder part, It gives us inward pain; But we shall still be joined in heart, And hope to meet again. Don’t you just love those old songs? Like… Down at the cross where my Saviour died, Down there for cleansing from sin I… There to my heart was the blood applied; Glory to His name! Glory… Prayer card number 70 is out, he says. Prayer card A-70… Glory to His precious name! Oh, there to my heart was the blood applied; Glory to His Name!

Someone holding prayer card 70…Would you check someone setting near you? It may be a deaf person. A-70, if they’re in the building, why, come take your place if you would while we sing this next verse. I am so wondrously saved from sin, Jesus so sweetly abides within, There at the cross where He took me in; Oh, glory to His name! Glory to His (precious) name! Oh, glory to His (precious) name! There to my heart was the blood applied; Glory to His…

I wouldn’t swap those songs for all the little choppy songs. I think they’re wonderful. Let’s sing just, “Glory To His Name,” the—the chorus. And just shake hands with someone setting near you, will you? Just turn around or something and shake hands. Come on now. Glory to His (precious) name! Glory to His (precious) name! Oh, there to my heart was the blood applied; Glory to His… Our heavenly Father, we thank Thee for Thy blessings, that we can sing tonight, “Glory To His Name.” For it was there at the cross where He took us in. Coming unworthy, all undone, naked, wretched, blind, spiritually speaking, and God in His tender mercy reached down and taken us as…alienated away from Him. And God cleansed us from our sins by the Blood of His Son Jesus Christ, and now has positionally set us in heavenly places with Him.

And now we are sons and daughters of God, joint-heirs with Christ in the Kingdom, setting in heavenly places, the Holy Spirit moving upon us. Oh, no wonder our hearts tremble when we hear those old fashion songs. Just makes us so grateful to You, Lord. Thank You. The writers of these old songs is with You tonight I…perhaps. God rest their gallant souls until they take body form again. Help us, Lord, as we sing them, to realize what they were meant for. Give us grace tonight, Father, and power of the Holy Spirit. And now, shut down as it was, all doubt; just shut it out of the building, Lord. And may faith rise and take its place, and may it be very predominant tonight. And may evil spirits leave the people, great joy be among the people, for we ask it in Jesus’ Name. Amen.

Let’s hum that once will you? [Brother Branham hums: “Glory To His Name”—Ed.] Oh, how I love that. That was one of the first songs touched my heart, cowboy playing it. [Brother Branham hums again.] Glory to His Name. God bless you. Trusting to Jesus Christ for our all tonight, believing that He is here with us, believing that He’s helping us, trying with His great love and mercy to inspire our faith in Him. That’s our only alternative: Try to find favor with the people, as God will let us, that their faith might be lifted up to believe in the Lord Jesus Christ more. We’re strangers. I do not know you. You perhaps don’t know me. ’Less it’s just by letter, or mail, or somewhere seeing me in the pulpit. But God knows us both. And knowing it is totally impossible for us to know anything of each other, no more than maybe, you’d know of me more, because you’ve read papers and so forth…But for me to know you…

Now, you look like a healthy woman. And you may be for all I know. That’s…God knows that; I don’t. But He has risen from the dead and living here with us tonight and has promised us that the things that He did that we’d do also. And He didn’t heal anyone, you know. He claimed He didn’t heal. No. He said, “The Father does it.” Is that right? But He—He knew their hearts, knew their thoughts. And He said, “I only do what the Father shows Me.” Could you imagine Him going through all those cripples there at Bethesda? And just think of those poor little water-head babies, and crippled, and spastics, and drawed up. And He never touched a one of them.

Walked right on over, and the man wasn’t too bad. He’d had maybe a prostate trouble or something, for about thirty-eight years. He was laying on a pallet. Jesus healed him. Then walked right on out of the building. Mmm. And they said He was full of love and compassion. His love wasn’t…It was to the Father. And as the Father would permit, He would do. He said the same thing in the 19th verse, you know. He said, “Verily, verily, I say unto you, the Son does nothing in Himself. But what He sees the Father doing, that doeth the Son likewise.” In other words, He does just what the Father shows Him. Now, if the Father tonight… Now, I believe as far as your healing, the Father has already got that in His glory tonight. Yeah. ’Cause He, when He gave Jesus, that purchased your healing.

Now, the only thing the Father could do…And then He sent His Word. Brother Baxter preached it very lovely and nicely tonight. Now, if there’s anything else could be done, there’s gifts set in the Church. Is that right? And then through there, God drops down, besides His love and His message of this Word, then He puts gifts in the Church that does different things. Now, there’s a gift in the Church…I believe Paul said, “If the— all of you speak with tongues and there comes in the unlearned, why, they’ll say you’re mad.” But said, “If there is one who prophesies and reveals the secrets to the people, then they’ll all fall down and say, ‘Truly God’s with you.’” Is that right?

Why such as that in a church tonight, don’t you think it ought to be sufficient for every person to accept Jesus Christ and believe Him? Yeah. Now, He’s risen. He is just like…We’re standing, talking like our Master and—and the woman at the well. Now, I’m doing this for a purpose. You know that. There’s lots of people out there, lots of believers. There’s literally hundreds of them. But they…I’m trying to contact you. Now, wasn’t nothing immorally wrong with the woman. I was just talking to her just a moment. I knowed that microphone’s alive. Now, you believe that God could show me what your trouble was, and whether it be anything, whether it’s domestic, or whether it’s— it’s—or whatever it would be, sickness or whether it…If you’re just curious, or whatever it would be, God could reveal it, couldn’t He? He could. Yes. You believe He could. All right.

But you’re not here just curiosity, because you’re really ill. Your trouble is in your chest. You have hurting in your chest. You’ve had an operation on that chest, is what’s caused it. It was a tumor operation or something. It was a—a growth in a breast and they removed it. Is that right? Now, if that’s…If God could reveal that…Now, what… Just what was it? Wasn’t it something about your—an operation or something? Something…Yeah, yeah. Breast…?…All right. All right. If that…If God can stand and do that through a worthless piece of flesh as we are, well, He’s Almighty, isn’t He? But He spoke through a mule one time and told a man something. And He—He spoke through a Cloud of Fire. He spoke through many…Just a moment.

You…Besides this, I see as you’re getting away from me again, going away. You have a very sad and lowly heart. You’ve—you’ve lost your husband, hasn’t it, sister? Are you convinced that Jesus Christ is near here now? You accept your healing from Him? May you and I have a word of prayer together? Our lovely Father, we thank Thee for Your mercies and kindness. And I pray for mercy for our dear sister. And may all the evil leave her. And may her heart rejoice and be made glad. And may she be healed tonight, and go to her home rejoicing. Now, may her faith have works with it. Grant it, Lord. In Jesus Christ’s Name, I ask it. Amen. God bless you, sister. Now, look we—we are strangers. Now, those things seem like I had a dream. See? But now what was said, was it the truth, whatever it was? If it was the truth, let the audience know by raising up your hand. It was the truth. I knew nothing of it, no way in the world for me to know it, is that right? We’re just perfectly total strangers.

Now, Jesus Christ is here. Jesus Christ healed the woman, and she can go home and be happy now. See? Why? Just because that she… Now, you’re going to be. Because you’ve come in the right attitude. No one ever come to Christ in the right attitude, but what went away with what they asked for: no one. See? Now, you go and you’re ju…If God could say what your life has been, God would surely know what your life will be, is that right? All right. Go on now. Forget all. Be happy. You’re going to rejoice and be happy. God bless you. All right. Come. I want to pray for these letters right now, before the anointing gets so deep upon me till I—I forget them. Now, heavenly Father, here’s some letters laying here. And they’ve got handkerchiefs in them. And they’re going to the sick and the afflicted. I pray for mercy, dear God. I pray that You’ll heal every one of them.

And I realize, Lord, that we’re unprofitable servants. There’s nothing in us that’s any good. But we think of what Jesus has commanded us to do. Oh, we just love You for that. And now, we’re taught that they’d taken off of the body of Paul, handkerchiefs or aprons, and unclean spirits went out of the people and they was healed of diseases. We’re not the Saint Paul, but You’re still Jesus. Now, we send these handkerchiefs in Jesus Christ’s Name, that everyone that these handkerchiefs touch, may they be healed for God’s glory, and the Glory of Jesus Christ, His Son. For we ask it in His Name. Amen. God bless you. (I think here’s two more, brother. Oh, they’re…Yes, sir. All right.) Good evening, sir. Do you believe on the Lord Jesus with all your heart, with all your soul? If our dear precious Lord Jesus would happen to come down in His anointing power and would reveal what is—what you’re seeking for, that would be the main thing that’d be on your heart, was what you’re seeking for. Whether it’s for…whatever it would be…No matter what it would be, He—He could reveal it (Is that right?) through His power. You believe that? Would you then accept, if He told you what to do about it? would you then accept it if He would reveal what’s wrong or what you want? And then He would tell you to do…You would accept His decision? Would that be right? May God bless you, my brother, I pray. I believe you’re coming humbly. I believe you’re approaching God in the way to receive something.

Yes, sir. Your—your trouble is in your heart. You have a—an enlarged heart. That’s right. And you also have dropsy, don’t you? Swelling, it gets real big sometimes, water just floods—separates in the water. Do you believe that He did make you whole when He died at Calvary for you? You now, while you’re standing on this spot here, in the presence of this company and before God, you now accept Jesus’ atonement there for your healing? Believe that you will get well and that heart will go down normal? If you’ll believe that with all your heart, before this meeting close, you’ll lay a—a ticket on this desk here, that your heart’s gone down and your dropsy’s left you. Will you do it with all your heart? O God, Creator of heavens and earth, send Thy blessings upon the man, and bring this to pass, for I rebuke this heart trouble, this swelling, whatever it is wrong with him. In Jesus Christ’s Name, may it leave him. Come out of the man. Amen. Now, go believing with all your heart, brother. God will make you well. Be in prayer now. All right.

Come please. Do you believe with all your heart, sister? You believe that Jesus Christ…If we would ask God…Now, it’s not only me praying, my sister, all those Christians are praying. And—and these back here, they’re all—and they’re ministers and everything, they’re waiting, wondering. And they’re wanting you to be healed. Do you believe that you will, when we ask God? Well now, just something to stimulate your faith. I could either—either, come over here and quote a Scripture, or I could give a testimony, or maybe God would come down and—and reveal something. Whatever He’d do, you would be thankful, wouldn’t you? You would.

And would there be a—a—enough evidence after hearing that sermon tonight, would it be enough evidence to you that you’re going to be made well? It would. If God would just tell you what—just reveal to me what’s wrong with you, then you—you’d—that’d be enough evidence for you that you’re going to be made well? Your trouble’s in your blood, is what it is, because between you and I, drops of blood are…And it looks white. You’re anemia. Is that right? Is that true? Then come here. Sister, by eyes of faith let’s look there to Calvary. And there was Blood sufficient, come from them, Emmanuel’s veins to give a blood transfusion by faith tonight.

O God, be merciful to this poor little woman. Lord, we’re just creatures of this earth, trying to get a—through, trying to live as long as we can to serve You. And I pray, as I lay hands upon this woman, according to a commission that was given to me by an Angel, that said, “If you be sincere when you pray and get the people to believe, nothing shall stand before the prayer.” And O great God, Who sent Him, may He now confirm the Word with signs following, as I’m laying my hands upon this little woman, and asking that she may be healed of this condition, in Jesus Christ’s Name. Amen. Now, sister dear, if your faith is just exactly where God said, I believe with all my heart that you’re going to be well. I believe it with all my heart. And you believe it too? Now, there can’t be nothing stand in your way. Now, just…Was you here last night when I was speaking on taking the Hivites and the…See? Just push them out of the way now and go on, thanking God for being healed. God bless you. We want to hear from you. All right.

Let us say, “Thanks be to God.” [Someone speaks to Brother Branham—Ed.] (Yes, sir. All right, that’s fine. If you…if I move out, you move me back, ’cause I—I forget about it, if you will.) How do you do, sister? You want to get over that diabetic condition, and go home, and be well, and be made well again? Would you like to do it? Come here just a minute. O Lord, Creator of heavens and earth, and this poor little mother standing here, looking at her little withered up hands, I think of my own mother setting there in the audience. And, Lord, no doubt, but what it’s wiped back the tears from a many crying baby’s face, probably done a many day’s washing.

And O God, maybe these little old fingers have thumbed through the Bible, and read the promises, and now Satan is trying to make her life just as miserable as he can. But we withstand him tonight by the promise of Jesus Christ. Now, Satan you leave the woman, as we lay hands upon her and believe with all of our heart that God’s Word is true, and you are a liar, and you’re defeated in Jesus Christ’s Name. Amen. Now, sister, go, and God’s peace be with you. Cause I believe you’re going to be well. You accept it now? Amen. God bless you. Oh… Oh, my. All right, sister, if you’ll believe God with all your heart, your eyes will never go out, and get well, and you’ll be all right. That’s your main thought tonight. Course you got some more things, as woman of your age, a female and so forth. But that isn’t nothing compared with what your eyes is. Your eyes is your main subject because they’re getting very bad. And it looks like you’re— may go blind.

But let’s look to that One Who’s anointed that man’s eyes with clay. He spit on the ground. And as he stood talking, He was spitting on the ground. And then He picked up that mud and spit, and rubbed it in His hands and plastered his eyes with it. What would the health authorities say about that today? See? But that was Jesus Christ. The man obeyed just exactly what he had done…what He told him to do and come back seeing. Is that right? Now, if you’ll obey just exactly what He said to do, you’ll receive yours too, and you’ll be well. You believe it? Let’s pray. Lord Jesus, now standing there in that little building that night, when the Light flashed across the floor and a great mighty Being come walking into that Light, trembling, I thought that maybe my time had come. But You said I was to go pray for the sick. And I’m doing it tonight, Lord, as faithfully as I know how.

Bless this one who I bless in Thy Name, and may the blind spirit leave her. May she get well. I pray this blessing in Jesus’ Name, and ask You, Lord, that her faith will not fail but she’ll go off this platform, so happy and full of the Holy Spirit, until she won’t even have to use glasses or nothing, and be perfectly well, in Jesus’ Name. Amen. God bless you, mother. God bless you. All right, would you come sir? Having faith? Believing with all your heart now. All right. Do that now. Would you like to get over the stomach trouble, son? and be made well? You would? Do you believe God’s Word is right? Do you believe that sermon tonight was right? Do you believe that I represent Him in a Divine gift, which knowed that—seen there that you can’t drink coffee and stuff like that. You have to scoot it back, because it sours on your stomach, got a acid condition? Is that right? Belches it up. Your teeth gets all sensitive. Sometimes you have to go out and vomit up what you’ve eat. Is that right? Exactly right.

Now, if the Holy Spirit’s standing here to make that known unto you, will you believe me as His servant? If you’ll go out of here and forsake that thing, just—just lay it aside, and go out rejoicing, and happy, and eat…No matter how you feel, eat anyhow, there’ll be a…after while, you’ll find out, you won’t have any stomach trouble at all. You believe me? Lord, may it come to pass; in Jesus Christ’s Name I ask it. Amen. God bless you, my brother. Go now, and eat anything you want to and have faith. Do you believe, sir? Just as you’re coming, walking like that, believe that God will make you well, just as soon as you get here and pray for you? You believe that with all your heart? Yes, I know you; I know what’s your trouble, but I—I’m just asking you a question. You will believe that it’ll do it? All right, come here.

O Almighty God, Author of Life, Giver of every good gift, send Thy blessings upon the man. And may his nerves quieten now. May he go off the platform here, Father, and be well. May he just take Jesus just now, and know that Jesus Christ is the all-sufficient Sacrifice. God is Jehovah-jireh, “the Lord will provide a sacrifice for Himself.” And now the sacrifice has been provided. May our brother accept it by faith and act it by works, in Jesus Christ’s Name. Amen. Now, go rejoicing, saying, “Thank You, Lord.” And be made well. All right, come. Believe it by faith. Act it by works. See? Act like it. You know, I may be wrong; and if I am, I pray, God forgive me. But I believe if I was sick and would walk up to a platform, and knowing I was a stranger to this person. And that person had been explained, and the Word had been laid out so carefully. And I’d watched it and seen how, nice it was laid out, and see it was absolutely fundamentally the Gospel truth. And then the Holy Spirit would be kind enough to me, to reveal to me just what I was asking for, like that. You know, I believe I’d jump off that platform, screaming. Now, that’s me. I…See? And remember, if you don’t believe with all your heart, don’t never get in that line. Cause it’d be better for you if you didn’t.

Because the Bible said, “Go ye and sin no more, or a worse thing come upon you.” And what is sin? Unbelief. When God has made Hisself manifested to you, like that. And you go away, “Well, I don’t know. He might’ve guessed that. It might…” Brother, it’s not guessing. See? No. And you go away like that, then just look out for something else to happen. That’s right. So don’t even come in the line. No matter what happens, you stay out of the line. If you don’t believe with all your heart that the works come from Jesus Christ. Just stay—stay out. And let someone come up who will believe. See? And to me, I’d—I’d think it would be the most happiest thing in the world, to know that…I know sometimes, I’m asking for something. And He will show me a vision. And I tell you, my wife thinks they got the Salvation Army in the bedroom, sometimes, when He reveals to me something another, that I’ve been asking for, for…And all at once, I look and here stands before me. And I see it unfolding to me, and I’ll scream and cry and I—I’ll tell you, I’m just so happy, I can’t hardly hold myself together.

And, it’s a wonderful thing. You believe that too, lady? If you’d get over that female trouble, would you be happy? Well, just go rejoicing, and say, “Thank You, Lord. Thank You, Lord,” and get over it. Amen. Let’s say, “Praise the Lord.” God, be merciful to us. Amen. How—how He is longsuffering, forbearing, not willing that any should perish, but all might come to repentance. Isn’t He marvelous? All right, would you come, lady, please. Just have faith now. Don’t doubt. Believe everything. And you’ll receive what you ask for, if you believe it.

How do you do, sister? Now, would…Do you believe if Jesus was here, standing here, wearing this coat, and a pair of trousers He gave me…If He was—if He was standing here, He would know what’s— what was wrong with you. But now, He’d have to do what the Father told Him. See? Well, now, I believe that if the Father would tell Him this, “Son, do You remember when You made that sacrifice at Calvary, You healed that woman.” See? Why, He’d say, “Yes, Father. Well then, I know I give a commission though. When I left the world, that they should go into the world and preach the Gospel and lay hands on the sick, and they’d get well.” I believe that would kind of be the conversation, don’t you thinks so?

Well then, if—if He’s here…But He’s working through His Church now; and we’re His Church. Then if I’d lay hands upon you, like He commissioned me to do, do you believe that arthritis would all leave you and you would be able to just to stomp your feet around and run home? Do you believe that? Then receive it in the Name of Jesus Christ. May it leave you. Now, come on. Jump your feet up-and-down. That’s right. Now, see, it’s all gone. Just go off the… Let’s say, “Thanks be to God.” Would you believe the same way if you were…?…Well, in the Name of Jesus Christ may you receive it and return back to your city rejoicing and being well. Amen. Now, go doing that with all your heart, just being happy and rejoicing and praising the Lord. Amen.

That’s the way friends. You’ve got to show God your appreciation. You know, if I would do something for somebody and I’d say…I’d have to make a great sacrifice like God did for us. And then, and somebody…I’d have my little check wrote out here to someone, and I—I’d say, “Here you are, brother, for your missions in the foreign fields or something.” He’d reach over, “Uh-huh.” I—I—I’d feel kind of bad, wouldn’t you? Oh, I’d expect him to say, “Thank you, Brother Branham. I—I know that really is taking what you got. You see? But I sure appreciate it, Brother Branham.”

And that’s the way God wants you to say, “Why, thank You, Father. I come up here to be healed, and it’s all explained to me. And You’ve proven it to me now. So I’m ready to go away from here rejoicing. Praise the Lord.” And go away just rejoicing and made well. That’s the way to do it. No matter if He wouldn’t say nothing at all, still you should rejoice, because the Word said so first. And that’s the initial, is that right, brethren? That’s the initial, the Word. All right, bring the lady. All right. Are you believing with all your heart? Little lady setting there, you got bowel trouble and rectal trouble, setting right back there. Isn’t that right? You was healed just a few minutes ago of that, in your seat. And you—you’re setting there; I— I was trying to wait. I tell you a little later on. But I was afraid I’d forget it.

Now, you go home and that’s going to stop. That dysentery and everything is going leave you. And—and it’s going to be all right, them hemorrhoids and things will go away and you’re going to be all right. God bless you. Have faith. That’s your faith now. I never prayed for you. Your faith has saved you. Your faith has made you whole. See, see? You didn’t have a prayer card to get in the line or nothing, ’cause there was no way for you to get here. But you just had faith. And God has healed you and made you well. So that—that’s just the way He does it. Amen. How do you do, lady? Do you believe with all your heart? You believe? Well, you believe that Jesus Christ is here to make you whole? You suffer with some sort of a—of a nervous condition. Isn’t that right? You’re very nervous, upset. Say, you’re not—you’re not from Chicago. You’re from out… you come from—from—from a way—from the east, coming here. Yes. All right. You believe He’s going to send you back well? You believe that? That’s right. Now, raise up your hands and say, “Thank You, Lord.” Amen.

Now, the nervousness is gone from you. You was made well standing right there. Return back to Buffalo, rejoicing and praising God. God bless you, sister. God bless you. Let’s say, “Praise the Lord.” [Congregation says, “Praise the Lord.”—Ed.] See? Never prayed for the woman, never touched her at all. I seen an airplane rise up. And I looked to the right hand side of the airplane where she looked from, and Niagara Falls was to the right, from where she raised up from. And I knowed she’d come from the east somewhere. ’Cause she was…passed by Niagara Falls. Is that right, lady? All right, sir. That’s right. It was in the vision just then. Amen. Hallelujah. Our Lord Jesus cannot fail.

Are you finished with that old kidney trouble and giving it over to God, and saying, “I’m going home and get well”? Believe it right now? You just go off of the platform, say, “Thank You, Lord Jesus,” and be happy. God will bless you and make you well. Never want to wear glasses, do you? You want to be well from that eye trouble, is that right? And you’re nervous and upset and so forth. All right. Believe Jesus healed you right where you’re standing? Go, in the Name of Jesus Christ, may the thing go out of you. Amen. Amen. Let’s say, “Praise the Lord.” You do the same thing, lady, you have the same thing. Now, go on just rejoicing. Yes, sir. That’s exactly. Go off and say, “Praise the Lord.” Just go rejoicing, happy, saying, “Blessed be the Name of the Lord.” Amen.

Oh, what we ought to do tonight, we ought to take this place by— not hold the fort but take the fort. Jesus Christ here, the Son of God… Now look, lady. Here. Come across there. Just let’s see you walk like a young lady. Come right on down there. That’s the time. Yes, ma’am. That’s the way. That’s the way I want you to do it. Amen. Praise the Lord. She’d been bothered so much, nervously too. And… You’re bothered with a nervous condition too, aren’t you, setting there on the—the end of the row? No. Your husband, setting next to you. Uh-huh! Yes, sir. You’ve been in the hospital, haven’t you? Spent two or three months over in a hospital, with a nervous breakdown, is that true? All right. You can go home and get well now.

Lady, you hit that lady. You—you’re some…connected with her. Is that right? You have arthritis, don’t you, the—the lady in the checked dress? You want to go home and get well too? Well, God bless you just…When the service is over, go down the street, singing: “Glory To His Name.” And just…Stand up. That’s right, brother. Stand up and give God praise. That’s right. Amen. Say, “Thank the Lord. Thank the Lord for His healing power.” Amen. Our Lord Jesus cannot fail. There’s no way for Him to fail. He is the Lord. Amen. Have faith now. Believe with all your heart and God will grant it.

It keeps moving…Are you two sisters there? And if God just… I…If you’ll just have the least bit of faith, lady, you—you’ll be healed tonight. See? You won’t never use them crutches no more if you just have faith now. All right, bring the—the lady on. Do you believe with all your heart? All your soul? All your strength? Excuse me. I—I was…See, I’m glad you said, “Yes.” That’s very nice. I…That’s what I want you to do is say, “Yes.” You believe God will make you well? Exactly. You have trouble in your chest too (Isn’t that right?), a hurting. You got a lot of troubles too, haven’t you? You’re now thinking about someone at home. It’s…I believe it’s a mother. You have a mother. She has a—a—a stroke, I believe it is. Or…Yeah. And you have one that…Have high blood pressure too. That’s right.

Say, by the way, aren’t you Catholic by faith? Is that right? I see the beads and things that…Do you believe that God will heal you, and make them well, and you go home happy, rejoicing and…Wouldn’t you like to have the—the fullness of God’s Spirit, to—to be filled with the Holy Ghost? Wouldn’t you like—wouldn’t you enjoy that blessing? Do you know it’s for you, sister? Jesus Christ died that you might have it. And I pray that you’ll receive the Holy Ghost before you leave this meeting. You know what the apostolic way of to receive the Holy Ghost is lay hands on them. And they received the Holy Ghost. And you’ll receive it. Do you believe that? Come here just a moment.

Almighty God, as this woman with her sincerity, standing here, believing that You’re going to make her well, I pray that You’ll heal her, and all that’s connected in this. And may she also receive the baptism of the Holy Ghost, Lord. May she be a testimony in this last days, to give praise and glory to God, in Jesus Christ’s Name. Go off the platform rejoicing, saying, “Thank You, Lord.” Amen. That’s the way. Amen. Some clergy ought to get to her immediately. All right, come if you will. All right. Do you believe with all your heart? Believe that God will make you well? That’s wonderful. All right. I want you…Have faith in God and believe with all your heart that God’s going to make you well. And that back will just smooth out and you won’t have that trouble no more. Is that right? It’s gone now. God has took it away from you. Move yourself down like this and see. See what I mean? Now, you go on off the platform and be happy. Your faith healed you, sister.

All right, come sir. Uncle, as you come do you believe that Jesus Christ, the Son of God, died to make you well? And He will heal you of that heart trouble if you will ask Him? Do you believe He does it now? Then say, “Praise the Lord.” That’s right. That’s the way to do it. Amen. Come, sir. That’s…Amen. Brother, I’m telling you, colored folks are not ashamed of their religion. I know that from being down in Africa, where—where they come from. Brother, let them see the power of God move once, and you don’t have to say no more. They got it and gone. Amen. Oh, shame on us. Amen.

Wouldn’t a nice big thick hamburger taste good tonight? You haven’t had one in a long time. Go on, eat it. God bless you. And may the Lord make…?…Amen. Hallelujah! Now, if that man could go off the platform, that colored man, rejoicing, healed with heart trouble, you ought to receive the same thing. God bless you. Go on. That’s right. Go on and believe with all your heart. Do you believe, lady? That old arthritis is gone from you. Go on off and show the people what the Lord has done for you. Amen. Amen. Get away from that heart trouble. Just move on across, saying, “Thank You, Lord. Thank You, Lord,” and be made whole. Amen. Do you believe with all your heart now? Lord Jesus, bless the woman, and heal her, I pray, in Jesus’ Name. Amen. Now, go rejoicing, saying, “Thank You, Lord Jesus. Thank You.” All right. Have faith in God. Amen. I…

God bless you, lady, setting there. You ain’t going to be bothered with that old sinus no more. It—it’s done gone from you now. Amen. Amen. God makes you whole, sister. God be with you. Hallelujah. You want to get over that rheumatism, setting there? You do? Just believe it, raise up; have faith in God and God will make you well. Amen. That’s all you have to do. Sister Wood, I thought that was you. But it isn’t. It’s the lady setting next to you there. She has a female disorder. And she’s nervous, kind of a nervous disposition. Something’s happened to her nerves. Isn’t that right, lady? You’re having a—kind of a little domestic affair. Isn’t that true? Well, God bless you. May He make you completely whole, take everything away, and make you exactly well. God bless you and give you peace.

Setting right back out there with that sinus, sir. If you want to get well, just raise up and accept it with all your heart. God bless you. He healed you just then. It’s all finished now. You can go home. God bless you. How do you do, lady? Do you believe me as God’s servant? All right, I want to talk to you just a minute, being that you’re the last one in the prayer line. Do you—you believe with all your heart? All right. Do you believe our Lord Jesus Christ is here in all of His lovely power and…

We’re strangers, I suppose. I—I don’t know you. Never seen you in my life. Anybody know the woman out there? Somebody? All right. People knows the woman. Then you know we’re strangers and that’s true. Now, our Lord Jesus is here. They’re…Why don’t we just accept it and say, “God I’m thankful. I’m going to accept mine right now.” All right. That’s right. You’ve come for a very good reason. You’re…I—I respect you and honor you, ’cause it’s…You’re barren, and you want children. Isn’t that right? You’ve heard; somebody told you about what happened and so forth. I have never asked that in my life but what God granted it.

Say, aren’t—aren’t you a min…No, your husband’s a preacher. Isn’t that right? All right. God bless you. And may the Lord grant to you your desire. God bless this little woman and make her fruitful, Lord. I pray that You’ll grant it in Jesus Christ’s Name. Amen. Amen. Who wants to be healed? Stand to your feet. Now, you wouldn’t have stood up ’less you had faith. Is that right? Now, if you’ve got works to—to go with your faith, raise up your hands and praise the Lord, just as loud as you can. Say, “Thank You, Lord Jesus.” And Father, I pray in Jesus’ Name that You’ll heal every one of them.

Thank you, Brother Boze. I could just have listened to that a while. That’s very fine. I’m sorry that I was late tonight. The manager called me up and told me to come a little early tonight. And I—I forgot about it. And I was just going ahead praying, and I happened to look up, and I think, “Well, here it’s…” I looked at my watch and I said, “Well, my it’s quarter after, I got to hurry.” And then here they was standing out there wanted to meet me when I come in. So they said they was going to dock me. So I guess that’s fine. All right.

Well, we’re happy to be here tonight. Very happy and sorry that the weather keeps on like this. But we understand that tomorrow or the next day, it’s going to break, according to the weather man. I hope that he’s right. But whatever, the Holy Spirit will meet with us just the same…?…He never fails us. And He—He will always be here just the same. I love Him tonight. And I know you do too, don’t you? [Congregation says, “Amen.”—Ed.] So I’m very happy that everybody’s in love with Jesus. And He’s in love with every one of us. That’s the good part, isn’t it? That He loved us before we loved Him. When we were real ugly behaving and contrary to God, yet He loved us. I just…That’s sounds bad, doesn’t it, to think that…? Brother Ryan, I don’t know whether I could suffer that very long or not, somebody being so ugly and different with me and still I love them.

Here one time, hasn’t been too long ago I was having a meeting in— up in Ohio. And oh, the big arena was packed and we was just…I had to stay way out in the country at a tourist court. And we’d been eating at a little Dunkard restaurant. Oh, it was the nicest people, and—and the people were so kind. And—and we appreciated them so much. And then Sunday, course they closed up. We had to go across the street, across the road, to a little place. It was a very worldly little place, had one of them little noisy jukeboxes that everybody played. Brother, the guy that’ll take them out of the nation, I’ll vote for him. I—I sure will. And all that there crazy music going on, and so as soon as I walked in over there, the first thing I noticed was a policeman standing with his arm around a young lady, playing a slot machine.

And that’s illegal in Ohio to play a slot machine. But the law… Now, then the next thing I noticed was, looked back there and a young lady very indecently dressed, and sitting on the side of the table about half drunk, and some boys with her… And looked sitting down to my right, there was an elderly lady about, oh, sixty-five, I guess. And she had a little very half nude clothes on, you know. And—and her lips was painted with blue-looking paint, and her toenails the same color. And uh, my, thought, “That’s terrible.” And I begin to think, “Is my little Sarah and Rebekah going to have to be raised up in such as that? What will be the outcome?” I thought, “O God how can you stand to look at it? Looks like You’d just turn on and blow the world up.”

And then while I was standing there looking at that, I was criticizing that woman. I was criticizing the officer in my heart. But I had never taken a seat yet at the table. And then just seemed like Something said to me, “Step over here to one side. I want to talk to you.” That was my Boss. And when I stood over there, and I begin to think like this. And it just seemed to come to me that—before me, not a vision, just a mental vision I’d call it. Seem like I could see the world. And around the world was a rainbow. And that rainbow represented the Blood of Jesus Christ. And if that Blood would ever leave there, God couldn’t look at the world a second. He’d destroy it. That Blood of Christ is the only thing that keeps the—the wrath of God off us tonight. Did you know that? If it wasn’t for that, there’d be no more world in five minutes from now. God cannot look in the face of sin. And the reason He can’t see the world is because the Blood of Jesus Christ is a holding it off of sin.

If God can look in and see such a scene as that, it’d be finished. He— He’s too holy. He couldn’t stand it. Then…But the Blood of Jesus… And then here’s what come to me. I thought to see the Blood of Jesus, how it acted as a bumper, just like to the car. The car instead of he strikes, it’ll hit the bumper and it, the—the bumper will protect the car. And I thought, “That’s what the Blood of Jesus is. It’s a bumper for our sins, that before it goes before God, it’s—He catches it. It’s a bumper.” And I thought, “Oh, my. Here I was criticizing that woman.” I may not have did that. I may not have act like that policeman was acting, but yet, in the sight of God I was a sinner, just as bad as they was, just as bad as the woman setting there. Sin is sin. That’s all. See?

No matter what your—your immorals are. You’re a sinner. You’re just a sinner. And so, I thought, “Yes, and God would’ve destroyed me if hadn’t been for the Blood of Jesus Christ, a keeping my sins from His Presence.” And then Something come to me and said, “Yes, I forgive you. But you want to condemn her.” I thought, “God, that’s right. That’s right.” I seen my sins then, and one day I crawled up to Him. And I seen an old Book laying there, had William Branham at the top and all kinds of sins wrote under it. And I said, “Lord, I’m—I’m so sorry that I’ve caused You all this bleeding,” and His face sweating and blood running down.

And I said, “I was the one who did that. Will You forgive me?” And He took His hand and dipped it in His side and wrote on that old Book “pardoned,” throwed It back behind Him in the Sea of Forgetfulness, never to remember it against me no more. That’s right. Now, He forgave me and I wanted to condemn her. That changed my attitude. I walked down there to the woman. I said, “How do you do?” There was two men with her, and they were very very bad acting. And so they just stepped out. And I walked down, and said I said, “Would you pardon me?” And she’s drinking. And she said, “Yes, sir.” I said, “I’d like to talk to you.” I said, “I’m a minister.” She said, “Yes?” And I said, “I am.” I said, “Wonder if I could ask you a question. Why does this, be like this? Are you a mother?” She said, “Yes, sir.” I said, “Why would you be drinking and things? May I ask if it’s not into getting personal with you?” Well, if you’d have heard the woman’s story, it was a heart broken story. And she said, “I was once a Christian.” Said, “If I’m not mistaken, aren’t you Rev. Branham that was down there?” I said, “I am.”

And I told her what I’d just seen. I said, “I stood here and condemned you, and thought God ought to come in and tear the place up, with such as this going on. But I’ve changed my mind. God forgave me. And I want Him to forgive you.” And right there at that seat, I led her to Jesus Christ. Amen. See? It’s your—it’s your attitude towards things. Don’t condemn others. If they do wrong, be good to them anyhow. Just look over those things. Because God’s had to look over a whole lot for you and I. That’s right. God help us to have that attitude always in our hearts. You pray for me that I’ll never look upon people like that no more. No matter what they’re doing. That I’ll always look up on them, that they’re creatures of God. That God sent His Son to take their place. And me as a minister, I’m grateful that He forgive me. And I want Him to forgive them also. That’s the way we should do it.

In Isaiah the 30, 53rd chapter we read this. Who has believed our report? and to whom is the arm of the Lord revealed? For he shall grow up before him as a tender plant, and as a root out of dry ground: he has no form nor comeliness; and when we shall see him, there is no beauty that we should desire him. He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrow, acquainted with grief: and we hid as it was our faces from him; he was despised, and we esteemed him not. Surely he has borne our grief, and carried our sorrows: yet we did esteem him stricken, smitten of God, and afflicted. But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquity: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed. All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way; and the Lord has laid up on him the iniquity of us all. He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he opened not his mouth: he was brought as lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is dumb, so he opened not his mouth. He was taken from prison from judgment: and who shall declare his generation? for he was cut off out of the land of the living: and for the transgressions of my people was he stricken. And he was…made his grave with the wicked, and in the rich in his death; because he has done no violence, neither was there deceit found in his mouth. Yet it pleased the Lord to bruise him; he hath put him to grief: when thou shall make his soul an offering for sin, he shall see his seed, and he shall prolong his days, and the pleasure of the Lord shall prosper in his hand. May the Lord add His blessings to the reading of His Word. The prophet Isaiah getting a vision of what Jesus was, Who He was, and what He would do, and what a sin offering He would make…

It’s awful warm tonight. So I believe instead of preaching as a I said I would. My preaching, and I’m not very much of a preacher. I’m just one of these old kind of sassafras we call it down in Indiana. You know. So you’re too nice of a people to have to push that off on. So I’ll just testify, and tell you something maybe that the Lord has did along our— our journey. And now, I want to think of some of my early days. When I first started in the great campaigns, the meetings had a lot of tinsel then. ’Course everybody was running here and there, but now, course it’s different than what it was then. But Pastor Baxter, my brother, and I were talking the other day, thinking, said, “Look at the great things, what’s happened, then look how it settles down.” God gives a meeting and then He finishes up His things. We think of Jesus Christ, when He was here on earth. His first years of His ministry, oh, the tinsel was hanging everywhere. The second year of His ministry, they had begin to accuse Him and call Him Beelzebub and so forth. The third year they killed Him.

See? That’s the way it goes always. The first years of the Pentecostal church, it was wonderful. Right away there was a persecution come in the second year and scattered them everywhere. The third and fourth years they begin to find people, just a little bitty groups: like there was five men besides four or five woman; that was a church. See how it is? It’s always that way. Just God sends out a great gospel net, and He throws it…The Kingdom of heaven is like unto a man who went to the sea and threw in a net. And when he drew the net in, he had everything that—that wallowed in the sea. He had it in the net. He had fish; he had turtles; he had water spiders; he had serpents; he had everything. Now, it’s not our business as preachers to say, “This is fish, and this is that.” We just pull the gospel net, and then it isn’t long when you see a revival go on, many people get saved and praise the Lord. But see, some of those are fish, and some of them are, we’d say, turtles. It isn’t very long till you’d say, “Well, I didn’t believe there was anything to it after all.” And here he goes running right on back into the puddle again.

The old water spider, you know. Plop, plop, plop: “Told you that wasn’t right after all.” Well, he goes back to the water. And the serpent will start hissing and saying, “I don’t like the way they do this things, sss-sss.” Right on back to the water it goes. But there’s some fish in there too. God knows. They’re fish by nature; he’s a spider by nature; he’s a serpent by nature.

And God is the One Who does the election and the calling. And it’s just our business to preach the Gospel. Is that right? God does the calling. One plants, another one waters, and God takes the increase. I remember it was a very hard thing at first when I first started out preaching Divine healing. Oh, my. I remember what the bishop of the church told me. Why, he said, “Billy, you had a nightmare. You never seen no Angel.” I said, “I don’t appreciate that, Brother Davis.” I said, “No, sir. It…To me it’s sacred. And it means a lots to me.” He said, “You mean you with your grammar school education is going to pray for kings and monarchs?” I said, “That’s what He said. It’ll be that way.” Said, “Go on, Billy.” And so. I said, “No, I’ll just give you my fellowship card while I’m standing here. Because I’m not going to be using it any more, I’m afraid.” So he said, “Oh, I wouldn’t think that way.” But I said, “Well, it we just may as well.” I said, “If God is sending me, there’s going to be somebody out there who’s going to receive it.” That’s all. God will never work anything here, but what He’s got something working there. And do you believe that? Absolutely.

I was…Today I was thinking, and a man in his heart, as he thinks in his heart, so is he. Then I was thinking of how that the first beginning of the meetings, after I got started out, the—some of the events that happened, how people would have dreams and come to the meeting, how a great revival was in its making and stirring. And now it’s just whirled out, went all around the world and everywhere. And tonight, even many of the Full Gospel churches are condemning Divine healing and saying, “There is no such a thing. It’s witchcraft and everything,” people who ought to be standing up for the—for the powers of God. But you know what God does? He just sets that organization on the shelf and moves on just the same. Doesn’t stop Him a bit. It’s always… All organizations will finally wind up over there in Babylon, just like the Bible says they will. And God out of the whole bunch…The very word “church” means “called out.” “Come out from among them, My people, that you be not partakers of their sins.” That’s exactly right.

Now, I remember one time in Jonesboro, Arkansas. As one of the— the thrilling things that just come into my mind now. It happened on a night…I was having services at the—the auditorium. And there’s so many people had gathered out there, till the paper said we had twenty-eight thousand. Well, if the paper said so, they were all there, every one of them. And so they was for forty miles near Jonesboro. You couldn’t even get a farm house. They had tent cities and everything, to—to take care of the people for the accommodations. When they began to see the marvel of God’s great power to reveal things, it was all new. They just went right out. But now they seen it so much till, “Well, Lord, if that’s all you got. Well, I will wait for something else.” Oh, my. That’s people, isn’t it? That—that’s people. But I remember I hadn’t seen my wife for about two months or three. And I had a little girl, my first little girl, which is, they’ll be on the road up here tomorrow. She’s seven years old now. She’s just a little bitty fellow when I left home. And when I come back, she didn’t even know me. I’d lost most of my hair, and I’d fell off a lot of weight, about twenty pounds and stoop shoulders. And her mother would tell her, say, “That’s daddy. (My picture on the—on the dresser.)” Said, “That’s daddy.”

And when I come in one cold day and walked into the place… And we lived in a little two rooms. And my wife was in there, and we was talking and she…I said, “Where’s the baby?” Said, “Asleep in the next room.” So I went in to the little old crib. And I never will forget; I woke her up. And those big blue eyes looked at me you know and she was scared of me. That hurt me. And I…Mother picked her up and handed her over to me. She said, “That’s daddy.” She got back. That wasn’t her daddy. She’d look over at the picture on the…Didn’t look like her daddy. So, well look, friends, I was preaching the Gospel. I was doing the best that I knowed how, as I’m doing tonight. Some glorious day it’ll be different over on the other side when we all get home. And I’d broke down. I was staying day and night in the platform, stayed one time for about four days and nights or more, without even leaving the platform, praying for the sick. And there were more people at the end of the meeting, many times more than there was when we started. And just no end to it, praying for the sick.

And great things were taking place. I remember one night there, there was a lady came up, she had her handkerchief like this. I thought she was crying. It was about three or four o’clock in the morning. And just as soon as I took a hold of her hand and was talking to her…I thought she was weeping. I said, “Oh, lady, you—you got cancer, haven’t you, on the nose? And she pulled it, the handkerchief back, and her whole nose was eaten off. And so…And I said, “Do you believe that Jesus will heal you?” And she said, “I have just left Memphis.” And she said, “The doctors told me over there the other day, there was no hope for me now. It’d done got such a straight start, rather till the radium or nothing would stop it.”

And oh, I thought, “Isn’t that…That sure is too bad.” And just a little bit after that, why, I prayed for her. And about three or four months from then, I was over at Texarkana, and was in a little meeting there. And the first thing you know, I seen somebody waving at me back there, and waving at me. And I didn’t know who it was. This young fellow jumped up; he was an exterminator at there. And he—he raised up. He said, “Brother Branham, I just can’t hold it any longer.” And I said, “What’s the matter, son?” And he said, “This is my mother. Do you recognize her?” I said, “No, I don’t.”

She said, “I was the woman who didn’t have any nose about three months ago.” She had another nose. God had healed her. It’d growed back. And I have her name and address and her testimony. And the trouble, the thing was she was doctoring, she went back to her doctor. And—and she said, he said, “Oh, my.” She said, “What did it look like now?” Said, “Why say.” Said, “What’s happened?” She said, “I changed doctors.” Said, “Well, who did you go to?” She said, “I went to Dr. Jesus.” He said, “Dr. Jesus?” Said, “Let’s see. Where does He practice at?” Said, “I don’t believe I…” My, isn’t that something? Oh, my. But many things happen along. I remember another night there that something taken place. I was at—at Little Rock and there was in a…Now, Rev. Mr. Brown…If you’d like for this testimony. Just write Reverend G. H. Brown, 505 Victor Street. V-i-c-t-o-r, Victor Street, in Little Rock, Arkansas.

We’d been praying and the, oh, the newspapers had give me the awfulest write up, saying that there was—that I’d blocked the…Had the ambulances out there. Said, “A Self-style nattily dressed Baptist preacher…” Oh, you never heard such in your life. I’m telling you. So they said…And they had the street cars blocked off in the streets from the ambulances. And I’d been praying for about two or three hours. And Rev. Brown come to me, which is one of the sponsors on the meeting. He said, “Brother Branham, when you get finished down at the bottom of the auditorium,” he said, “there’s a case like you never seen before.” I’d been praying for the sick then about three or four months, seen many things in that much time. And he said, “When you get a chance to take a little breath…” I was going to pray for them all night anyhow. Said, “Come down. I want to show you something like you’ve never seen before.” And I said, “All right.” So after while I went down to the steps. And now, friends, when I got down…

I’m just telling these things for God’s glory (You see?), for the glory of Jesus Christ, that you might know some of the things that’s happened. Oh, millions of things, oh I wouldn’t say millions, but many thousands of things anyhow has happened. And I went down at the bottom of the steps. And there laid a lady, laying on the floor. She was dressed with like shorts. And she had both hands sticking up like this and her feet sticking right up, laying on her back, just laying there like that. I said…There was a typical old Arkansas brother standing there, and he… I said, “Is that your wife?” He said, “It is, Brother Branham.” I said, “Why is her—her—her leg’s bleeding like they are?” Said, “Well…” Said, “She’s from the insane institution.” Said, “She was going through the time of menopause. And she had a baby born, and it threw her into a premature menopause. And the doctor give her some shots, and it went to her head. And so she went wild.” And he’d been in the insane institution two years. And he’d heard about from over in Mississippi a—a soldier’s mother that’d been healed and taken out of the institution. So, he said, “I brought her.”

Said, “Brother Branham, I’ve got four little children at home.” And he said, “And I’ve—I’ve, we’ve sold our farm and everything,” he said, “to—to try to get her well. And she’s taking treatments.” And said, “Then today,” he said, “I—I sold my mules.” He said, “I had to bring her down here.” And said, “They let me bring her out, just over the night.” And said, “They couldn’t get her in an ambulance. And I’d taken some brothers up there. And five of us got her out of the place and put her in a car.” And said, “That’s where she kicked all the glasses out of the car coming down, where five men couldn’t hold her.” And when they got her in the building there. Brother Brown said she’d just taken the place. They’d just, she’d just throw men every way. So when they’d let her down though, she’d lay on her back and just throw her hands and feet up like that, her eyes set real glassy. And that’s the way she stayed. Why, I said, “That’s too bad.” I said, “I’ll walk out and take a hold of her hand.” He said, “Oh, Brother Branham, don’t you do that.” Said, “She’d kill you.” Oh, I said, “I don’t think so.” And I…And it just a boy like on the way, so not having too much dealing with demonology. So he said, “Brother Branham, I warn you. Don’t do that.”

And I said, “Oh, I don’t think she’d hurt me brother.” And I walked down a little step like that, walked out on the floor. And she was laying there with her hands up. I said, “How do you do, sister?” Took a hold of her hand. And just as I took hold of her hand, I…she just gripped down like that. And she gave a pull like that. And she pulled me practically off of my feet. And she would’ve threw me across the room. And I… Why, she would’ve weighed about a hundred, and, oh, I guess seventy or eighty pounds, and that demon power… Did you ever see a person possessed with demon power? They got four times their strength. Well, if the devil can give you four times strength when possessed with him, what about possessed with the Holy Ghost? How much power could God give you? See?

And then…That’s the reason you’re afraid, you people that’s crippled. Don’t be afraid. Fling away them crutches, and get up and start off. God’s with you. If He’s anointed you, He will give it to you. That’s right. Be anointed with the Holy Spirit. And then, when this woman, she jerked me like that. And I almost come off of my feet. And I threw my ha…foot like that and caught her right across the breast like this. I caught…And it pulled my hand out of hers. Well, I—I ran back towards the—the steps again. He said, “I told you, Brother Branham.” And she started making a real funny noise, going, “Hee-hee, hee, hee-hee. Hum-hum, hum, hum-hum.” And she started crawling like a snake on her back, just a real…You could hear dragging, you know, just drag, drag, like that across the floor, concrete like that. And she got against the wall, put her great big strong limbs against the wall, and kicked like that, and when she did she hit a—a seat and her head hit like that. And it…There’s a seat setting there where the people had been sitting in before they brought her there.

And it broke the seat, the bench it was. And the hair and blood come out of her head. She just started making real funny noise, picked up that thing in her hand like that and threw at her husband, and just knocked the plaster off the wall where it hit right by the side of where he was at. Said, “You see, Brother Branham,” said, “now all hopes is gone.” Said, “What can I do?” And he…The poor old fellow started crying, put his arms up around me like that, old patched overalls on. I felt so sorry for the boy. And I said, “Well, brother, look: the only thing I know to tell you that this Angel that met me told me that, if I be sincere and get the people to believe when I prayed, that He’d heal the sick.” I said, “Do you believe that, the simple faith to believe that Jesus Christ, the Son of God, cast out devils? And He—He has gone up in to the Father now, and He’s here in the form of the Holy Spirit.” I said, “I believe He’s the same Jesus today that He was then.” I said, “I don’t have to tell you what’s wrong. You know what’s wrong.” He said, “That’s right.”

I said, “Do you believe if I’ll ask God, God will do it?” He said, “I do.” And about that time she turned around on her back. She said, “William Branham, you haven’t got nothing to do with me. I brought her here,” come crawling up towards me. Why, her husband turned, said, “What’s this?” Said, “That woman don’t even know her own name.” Said, “She hasn’t spoke a word in two years.” I said, “That wasn’t her. That was that devil. See? That’s that the devil. He knows that he’s going to have to leave the woman if you’ll only believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, right now.” And he kept calling like that. “You have nothing to do with me. I brought her here.” So I said, “Now, you agree with me.” He said, “All right.” I said, “Heavenly Father, in the Name of Your Son Jesus Christ make that devil leave the woman.” So she didn’t never talk no more. She just…He said, “What shall I do?” I said, “Take her on back after service is over. If you believe, it’s got to happen.” He said, “All—all right.”

So about three months after that, I was up here at—at Jonesboro. And I happened to see somebody back there waving. And I didn’t know who it was, sitting right out like that. And they was waving at me. And it was—it was the woman sitting there. She said, “Don’t you recognize me, Brother Branham?” I said, “No, I don’t.” She had her four little children all sitting around. She said, “The last time you seen me, they told me that I was bleeding all over and I was out of my head.” And the…He had took the woman back, had no trouble taking her back. She set up. And the second day, when she was in the institution…I said, “Let them dismiss her.” So the second day, they come to her and she was sitting up. The third day they give her a discharge from the place, sent her home in her right mind. See? That’s right. Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever. Isn’t that nice? But I had just about a time for about another little short testimony?

My wife had never seen one of the meetings. And I sent for her to come down. I was so lonesome. And so she came down. And Brother Reed…This was at Jonesboro. And Richard, T. Richard Reed could give you the testimony of this. The Blessed Old Bible Hour Tabernacle, he’s the pastor of it, down in Jonesboro, Arkansas, if you’d like to get this testimony. And then, I remember that night when we started the meeting, for three city blocks standing in the street, you couldn’t…The cops was there, just letting them as they would pile up like that and block off the sides. And keep a… And my wife said, “Did all these people come to hear you preach, honey?” I said, “No, honey, they come to see Jesus.” And the little fellow stood there. She’s very backward, holding my hand crying. And she sang this song: Oh, they come from the East and West, They come from the land afar, (You’ve heard it.) To feast with the King, to dine as His guests. How happy these pilgrims are!

And she was standing there singing that for me. And then the ushers come forth and said, “Brother Branham, they been waiting.” And so down…I never knowed what become of her. And they got me into the building. And just as I got in there, I happened to look down. Oh, the ambulance stretchers and everything laying. There’s two nurses by a little girl here. She had TB. And I—I could just feel that something was going to take place right there. And while I was watching it, there was a man standing over on this side with a blue uniform, kept waving his hat. I said, “Are you trying to talk to me, sir?” He said, “Yes, sir.” Said, “I’ve—I’ve got a case out here that’s and—and she’s dying. And I think she’s already dead.” Said, “I can’t find a doctor anywhere.” And said, “We had a doctor there, just a house doctor.” And said, “I think she’s already dead.” And said, “Would you come to her?” I said, “Brother, there’s probably two thousand people backed in there.” I said, “I don’t believe I could do it.” And—and four or five ushers stepped down and said, “Well, we’ll help you get up there.” We started out, and got out to the ambulance where…Oh there was about eight or ten ambulances setting in the row. And this is a big ambulance.

The—the man told me said, “There’s been a man had been healed that morning, blind, been blind for ten years. And he was prayed for, told him he was going to receive his sight. And on the road home that morning, his eyes come open.” And his…He was riding an old Model T Ford up them rough roads in Arkansas. And he begin to scream. They stopped the car and out and around and around the car he went screaming. He run into the city, Kennett, or some little place down in Missouri, that little boot hill type of Missouri there. And he run went into the church, the Catholic church, and begin to testify, and they throwed him out. And—and he had his hat hanging on his black cane like or his white cane, rather, his black hat, going down the street screaming to the top of his voice, used to be a shoe cobbler there. And he was going down the street, screaming and praising God. He went into a Methodist church. Ha-ha. They throwed him out of there. They didn’t know…He was taking the city. Now, I tell you, he was… And they had a everybody in the hospital wanted to come down and be prayed for. So, the ambulance said, “I’ve got to go back.” And said, “I’ve—I’ve got to…” So we got in there and when he… I said, “Well, now you just open the door.” We went in and a very typical old dad there, his old hat sewed with twine, wrapping string, you know, around…

Those Arkansas people are poor as they can be. But brother, under them old blue shirts beats some real good true Holy Ghost filled hearts. Yes, sir. I’d rather have one of them with me any time, than maybe a slicker with his collar turned around in the back, and I couldn’t trust him out of my sight. Yes, indeedy, yes, indeed. Just…I tell you, this old time religion, brother, it straightens you up. That’s right. It’ll make a—a—a silk dress and a calico put their arms around one another and call “sister.” Is that right? It’ll make a tuxedo suit and a pair of overalls call each other “brother.” That’s what it’ll do, brother. It’ll clean you up. It’ll make no difference in you. It tears down that self, and starch, and pride, that we’ve got.

And so, then I—I remember getting in there, and he had the soles of his shoes was out. He was kneeling down hollering, “O God, give her back to me, God.” Poor old fellow. I happened to think of my own old dad when I see him gripping that hat like that. I said, “What’s the matter, dad?” He said, “Who are you?” And I said, “I’m Brother Branham.” He said, “Oh, Brother Branham,” said, “mother’s such a sweet woman.” And said, “I’ve lost her, I’m sure.”

And I said, “Well, what’s the matter?” So I took a hold of her hand. And her eyes were set now, but I do not think she was dead. See? And her false teeth had been taken out, and laying down. And like muddy looking water would come down from her eyes. And her eyes were set right back. Real old woman, not real old, but passed the middle age, I’d say sixty-eight seventy, somewhere along there. So she was laying and—like that. And I said…And I felt of her. Her forehead was sticky with perspiration. And he said, “She’s just quit breathing a while ago, Brother Branham.” Said, “Oh, she’s a good woman.” Said, “She’s harrowed over them old clods and helped to make me a living.” Said, “We raised a bunch of children.” And said, “She took this cancer.” And said, “The doctor has worked faithfully. He’s done all he could do.” It was in the female glands. And said, “There’s nothing more he could do.” And said, “We sold her quilts to get the ambulance to bring us down here,” the quilts that she had made.

I thought, “O God.” I said, “Well, let’s pray, brother.” And I took a hold of her hand. And I said, “Heavenly Father…” I was going to pray for consolation. I’ll confess it. I thought the woman was gone. And so…I…And it was while I was praying I felt something grip my hand. The devil said to me, said, “That’s just the flesh you know. Just she’s dead and that’s just the nerves twitching.” And I went ahead praying a little bit longer, and I felt it twitch again. I looked. I kept praying. But I was looking over at her. And the old man was down on the floor crying, “God, give me back mother.” And I was holding her hands like that. And then I happened to look again. And I seen the—the skin on her forehead wrinkling. And she looked up at me. She said, “What’s your name?” And I said, “I’m Brother Branham.” She said, “Well, we come down for you to pray for me.” And I said, “Yes, ma’am.” She said, “I feel so good.” I said, “Would you set up?” And about that time he looked, and the old man looked at me hollered, “Mother, mother, mother!” the tears running down his poor old whiskered cheeks. And he—and he grabbed like her and they begin to hug and kissing one another. And oh, three or four months later, she was in the meeting down there testifying, just shelling the woods with that testimony.

So I started to go out and the usher said, “Why, Brother Branham you couldn’t get out.” Said, “There’s thousands of people that’s banked in here.” And so I said, “Well, if you’ll just act like you’re taking off your coat now. They won’t notice me and I’ll slip out this other side. And you send them ushers around. Nobody knows me back there in that parking lot,” just standing full of people, and it raining, just pouring right on down. They was standing out there anyhow, holding papers over their children and things like that. Been laying on the streets for five or six days at a time, like that. Laying under cotton trucks, anything they get…They love the Lord. They come to church. Brother, they love Him and they believe Him. And then I was…went around the back of the place, like that. He started to…That looked like a hypocrite to do that. But I just couldn’t get in to where they was all at. And the poor things just almost stampede you. So, he started taking off his coat like this. And I slipped out the door and went up, down through that ambulance row, come around in the back, and started in up there.

There was…Big flood lights was back in behind the place. And they had a bunch of chartered buses setting like that. And I was going along through there, pushing along, you know, like this. And nobody knew me; nobody had seen me yet. ’Cause they couldn’t get near the building. They’d stay right in that building. What was in there, kept their places. And so they send someone out to get some sandwiches, or somebody hold their place while they had to got out and come back, you know. They was holding their place. Then I—I was thinking as I went along there. Somebody kept saying, “Quit pushing. Quit pushing.” I said, “Excuse me.” Just kept on, you know, pushing along. I pushed up beside of a great big tall fellow, standing there whittling with his knife. And I pushed right under him like that. He said, “Quit pushing.” I—I did, because I was afraid he was going to push. And so I—I said, “Excuse me, sir.”

And I—I stood with my hands down like this. He looked down at me kind of sarcastic like, you know, and kept on whittling. I said, “I’m sorry.” He never said a word, just kept on whittling. Yes, sir. I watched, and I thought, “Well, I’ll start pushing again in a few minutes when he gets to thinking about something else.” So I looked around. And so after while I heard somebody hollering, “Daddy! Daddy!” I wonder where that was. It sound like a southern voice of the colored people. Usually they all the Southerners talk a whole lot alike. And I happened to look, and coming out in the midst of people, more than there is setting here, standing in that back parking lot, was a young colored girl. Now, down there they have a law of segregation: Jim Crow law. And the white and colored cannot come together. And so…I don’t think that’s right. But as so that’s—that’s wrong. I just don’t say that for any respects for our colored friends here tonight, but I don’t care if there’s nobody here. That’s wrong. That’s right.

And I’m a Southerner, but I—that’s still wrong. I’m a Abraham Lincoln man. I—I believe that—that God made us all the same. That’s right. So then…And I seen the girl coming, and—and I seen her—her eyes was as white with cataracts as my—my shirt. And she was… Nobody would help her. She was just pushing through the crowd hollering, “Daddy! Daddy!” like that. And I thought, “Poor old thing.” And I thought, “I believe I’ll get over to see what she wants. Nobody knows me.” And I was watching for those ushers to come around the corner. They was trying to get through the crowd. So I pushed up close to where she was. And when started this way, I’d get over this way. So I’d get right in front of her. And so that looked like awful to do that. So she bumped right in to me. She said, “Pardon me.” I said, “Yes, ma’am.” She said, “Pardon me, sir.” When she heard my voice of being a man. And I said, “What’s—what’s the matter?” She said, “Sir, I’ve lost my daddy. I can’t find him.” Said, “I’s blind. And I can’t find my daddy.” And I said, “Well, where you from?” She said, “I’m from Memphis.”

And I looked over, and I seen the chartered bus setting there from Memphis.
